# Pricing & promotion recommendation

*Generated by `python -m fdda.analysis.discount` (full data). Every number is read
from `reports/discount/*_full.csv` and `discount_summary_full.json`.*

## Summary

Across 104,547 H&M articles and 31,788,324 transactions, **no discount band earned more margin per article-week than full price** under any of the assumed gross margins. Once an article is marked down, **margin per week peaks in the 15-25% band (median discount 20%) and falls sharply beyond it (25-35% onwards)**, the same under all 50%–70% margin assumptions. Myntra's cross-sectional revenue proxy also peaks in the 15-25% band.

## Recommendations

1. **Cap routine markdowns at the 15-25% band (about 20% off).** Going deeper cut margin per article-week from 0.80 to 0.51 of full-price margin in the next band (60%-margin scenario) without a matching lift in units.
2. **Avoid token discounts in the 5-15% band.** They sold 0.85× the units of nearby full-price weeks and kept only 0.74 of full-price margin: margin is given away without extra volume.
3. **Reserve discounts beyond 15-25% for clearance.** At 55%+ the margin index is -0.00 (60% margin). Deep cuts can still be right for end-of-season stock with no other exit, but that is an inventory decision (holding cost, salvage value) this data cannot value, not a demand-generation tool.
4. **Use category-specific caps** (table below): cap Shoes and Swimwear at a shallower band (5-15%); the other categories follow the overall pattern.
5. **Tie promotions together:** win-back offers in the customer playbook (Phase 4) are capped at the same 15-25% band.
6. **Validate with a controlled test** before rolling out (design below).

## What was measured

* **Data:** H&M transactions, 31,788,324 units over 2,210,899
  article-weeks (104,547 articles). Prices are normalised, so revenue is an index.
* **Discount:** 1 − price ÷ reference price, where the reference is the 95th percentile of the
  article's price over a trailing 8-week window (13%
  of article-weeks fall back to the article's lifetime max because the window is thin).
* **Comparison:** for each article, units, revenue and margin per week in a discount band divided
  by the same article's full-price weeks within ±8 weeks (a *local* baseline, because
  markdowns come late in an article's life when demand has already faded). Medians across
  articles.
* **Margin:** no cost data exists, so unit cost = (1 − m) × reference price for assumed
  full-price gross margins m = 50%, 60%, 70%.
* **Ceiling:** the last band before each extra discount point *lowers* the margin index.

## Results by discount band (all articles, local baseline)

1.00 = the same per week as the article at full price.

| Band | Articles | Median discount | Units / week | Revenue / week | Margin / week (50%) | Margin / week (60%) | Margin / week (70%) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0-5% | 91,145 | 0% | 1.00 | 1.00 | 1.00 | 1.00 | 1.00 |
| 5-15% | 67,378 | 10% | 0.85 | 0.78 | 0.72 | 0.74 | 0.76 |
| 15-25% | 61,469 | 20% | 1.06 | 0.92 | 0.74 | 0.80 | 0.84 |
| 25-35% | 37,495 | 29% | 1.00 | 0.70 | 0.41 | 0.51 | 0.58 |
| 35-45% | 35,698 | 40% | 1.10 | 0.77 | 0.27 | 0.45 | 0.57 |
| 45-55% | 35,245 | 50% | 1.09 | 0.68 | 0.01 | 0.25 | 0.41 |
| 55%+ | 31,644 | 61% | 1.00 | 0.50 | -0.26 | -0.00 | 0.16 |

* **Discounts barely lift weekly volume.** Units per week stay within 0.85–1.10× of full price
  across bands, so revenue and margin fall with depth.
* **Elasticity** (log units on log price ratio, article + week + article-age fixed effects):
  β = -0.08 [95% CI -0.09, -0.07],
  i.e. a price 10% further below the reference price is associated with about
  0.8% more units. Without the age control β =
  0.01: lifecycle decay hides part of the discount effect.
  Under a constant elasticity of this size, the implied margin-optimal discount is
  0%.
* **Sensitivity:** with the plan's *lifetime* baseline the markdown ceiling is
  15-25% (the same), and discounted bands sit further below full price, because late-life markdown weeks are compared with launch weeks.

## Ceiling by category (once marked down)

| Category | Ceiling (60% margin) | Margin index at ceiling | Ceiling at 50% | Ceiling at 70% | Elasticity β [95% CI] |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Socks & Tights | 15-25% | 0.92 | 15-25% | 15-25% | -0.01 [-0.07, 0.05] |
| Nightwear | 15-25% | 0.79 | 15-25% | 15-25% | -0.17 [-0.26, -0.07] |
| Underwear | 15-25% | 0.93 | 15-25% | 15-25% | 0.08 [0.03, 0.13] |
| **All articles** | 15-25% | 0.80 | 15-25% | 15-25% | -0.08 [-0.09, -0.07] |
| Garment Full body | 15-25% | 0.79 | 15-25% | 15-25% | -0.14 [-0.16, -0.11] |
| Garment Lower body | 15-25% | 0.79 | 15-25% | 15-25% | -0.03 [-0.06, -0.01] |
| Garment Upper body | 15-25% | 0.82 | 15-25% | 15-25% | -0.14 [-0.15, -0.12] |
| Accessories | 15-25% | 0.79 | 15-25% | 15-25% | -0.08 [-0.11, -0.06] |
| Swimwear | 5-15% | 0.74 | 5-15% | 5-15% | 0.24 [0.19, 0.28] |
| Shoes | 5-15% | 0.77 | 5-15% | 5-15% | -0.11 [-0.15, -0.06] |

Elasticity β < 0 means deeper discounts go with more units. Positive values (seen in seasonal
categories) reflect end-of-season clearance: the items discounted in a given week are the ones
that are not selling.

| 0-5% | 201,523 | 20% | 1.00 | 1.00 |

## Limitations

* **Not causal.** Markdowns are not random: slow sellers get discounted, and timing follows the
  season and lifecycle. Fixed effects and the local baseline remove the main confounders, and the
  remaining bias most likely makes discounts look *less* effective than they are (weak articles
  are the ones being discounted).
* **No zero-sales weeks.** Weeks in which an article sold nothing are not observed.
* **Normalised prices and assumed margins.** Revenue is an index; margins are scenarios.
* **No inventory data.** The value of clearing stock is not counted, which matters most for
  deep end-of-season discounts.

## What an A/B test would add

Randomise markdown depth for comparable articles at the same lifecycle stage, e.g. 0% / 10% /
20% / 30% assigned by store cluster or customer cohort for 4–6 weeks, holding the article set
fixed. Measure units, margin per article-week and sell-through, and confirm whether the
15-25% ceiling holds once selection and timing are removed by design.

## Reproduce

```bash
make clean-data            # FDDA_MODE=full for all customers
FDDA_MODE=full make discount
FDDA_MODE=full make payback-notebook   # notebooks/02_discount_payback.ipynb
```
